title: ci: select affected verification inputs and preserve historical replays
head: b15a55ba1cecf985a584ad5926bc67ebb940b8d3
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Every revision currently launches the full artifact matrix and four unfiltered
package workflows, including checks whose inputs did not change. This change
selects affected groups from declared, runtime-checked inputs, retains every
supported Python combination for selected groups, adds superseded-PR cancellation
and a stable `verify-summary` gate, and caches pinned Mathlib dependencies.
Scheduled/manual/full-label runs retain complete coverage. Unknown paths and
changes to shared verification code run everything.

The independent audit fixed label events producing empty successful gates,
failed trace recordings losing their failure status, cancellation API errors
being ignored, and missing external inputs in the historical formal declaration.
The complete historical formal target has now been traced successfully.

Historical clone/split checks also replay authenticated predecessor source bytes
in private copies, fixing pre-existing source-pin failures without reverting the
current optimized implementations or weakening frozen evidence. This is CI
maintenance; no selected frontier, mathematical claim, source pin, archive or
upstream source is changed.

## Task and overlap

Explicit task: reduce CI queue/load and audit the changes before submission.
Base: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` from canonical main.
Scope remains CI maintenance; no research task was drawn.

The existing optional speedups in #1041, #1059, #1151, #1433 and #1584 remain
opt-in and byte-unchanged. #2214 concerns selected-result navigation; this change
addresses execution selection and historical replay compatibility. See
`docs/ci.md` for dependency semantics, timing methodology, historical sources,
required-check guidance and validation limits.

Replaying the selector over 60 recent PRs gives an estimated mean workload of
63 runner-minutes versus 232 previously. These use old per-job durations and
exclude new tracing/copy/summary overhead; they are not a hosted speedup claim.

## Validation

Validation was run in an isolated worktree, with artifact suites sequentially.
Linux x86_64, Python 3.14.4, pinned Lean 4.21.0 / Mathlib
`308445d7985027f538e281e18df29ca16ede2ba3`.

- Workflow lint: `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml`.
- Planner, tracer, historical overlay, cancellation and selected-input controls.
- Complete traced `clones` group: native reconstructions, 4,073,300 fixed-basis
  pairs, historical witnesses and 21 package tests.
- Complete traced historical formal target: 45 ranked-pair theorem audits,
  298 machine-transfer declaration audits, Lean build, 386 project axiom audits,
  source/literal checks and paired-circuit reconstruction.
- Final complete traced tests group: all 130 modules, all 20 patch-application
  checks and the declared-input coverage audit passed.
- Selected record/input checks and tracked-artifact drift checks.

Reproduction commands and local-only evidence locations are in `docs/ci.md`.
Hosted runs and Python 3.11/3.13 execution have not yet been verified. The selected
cold replay was not rerun because its construction and pinned inputs are unchanged.
No live backlog cancellations or branch-protection changes were performed.
These scoped checks do not formally verify the full multiplication theorem.

## Credit

Sagar Thakrar, with substantial Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI Codex assistance,
including independent code reviews. The authenticated historical adapter builds
on Dennis's prior work and preserves its source attribution. Wentao Li's live
circuit optimizations and equivalence controls remain unchanged. Original
snapshot headers, contributors and Apache-2.0 licensing are retained.

## Open next questions

Measure hosted end-to-end duration and queue recovery after deployment. This is
maintenance tooling, not a new research package.
limits: Metadata and source identity only. Checks require source/command/coverage review; no green-badge inference.
